name: a_index_closes
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Index closes & futures.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, Dow, Russell 2000, PHLX SOX closes (level, % change); S&P sector leaders/laggards; biggest index point contributors; index futures pre-market on the brief date (% change, time quoted).

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Index Closes — Friday, October 2, 2026 `[Macro / Calendar]`

- **S&P 500** closed at **7,722.72**, up **56.27 points, or 0.73%**. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 15:23 ET)[13]
- **Nasdaq Composite** closed at **27,190.86**, up **319.27 points, or 1.19%**. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 15:23 ET)[13]
- **Dow Jones Industrial Average** closed at **51,176.96**, up **250.40 points, or 0.49%**. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 15:23 ET)[13]
- **Russell 2000** rose **26.27 points, or 0.9%, to 2,832.90**. (Associated Press via Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2; publication time not stated)[2]
- The **PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX)** closing level and percentage change were not included in the available search results.

## S&P 500 Sectors `[Macro / Calendar]`

- **Consumer discretionary** led S&P 500 sectors, rising **more than 1%**; **materials** and **information technology** also rose **about 1%**. (Investor’s Business Daily, Oct. 2, 16:39 ET)[1]
- **Health care** was the only S&P 500 sector to decline; the other **10 sectors** advanced. (Investor’s Business Daily, Oct. 2, 16:39 ET)[1]
- The **S&P 500 real estate index** gained **0.4%**. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 15:23 ET)[13]

## Index Point Contributors `[Macro / Calendar]`

- **Nvidia** and **Tesla** were identified by Reuters as significant positive contributors to the S&P 500’s advance; individual index-point contributions were not provided in the available results. (Reuters, Oct. 2; publication time not stated)[10]
- **Cisco** rose nearly **3%**; **Caterpillar**, **Nvidia**, **Alphabet** and **Amazon** each gained **1% or more** within the Dow. (Investor’s Business Daily, Oct. 2, 16:39 ET)[1]
- **Nike** fell about **3.5%**, making it the leading Dow decliner after forecasting a larger fiscal-year sales decline than analysts expected. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, publication time not stated)[6]
- **Seagate Technology** and **Western Digital** closed with heavy losses, while **Nvidia** reached a record high. (Investor’s Business Daily, Oct. 2, 16:39 ET)[1]

## Index Futures — Monday, October 5, 2026 `[Macro / Calendar]`

- At **10:40 p.m. ET on Sunday, October 4**, **Dow futures** were up **0.01%**, **S&P 500 futures** were up **0.08%**, and **Nasdaq-100 futures** were up **0.27%**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 5, 00:17 ET)[7]
- In a pre-market reading published at **07:19 ET**, **S&P futures** were at **7,788.00**, up **10.75 points, or 0.14%**; **Dow futures** were at **51,502.00**, up **25 points, or 0.05%**; **Nasdaq futures** were at **31,181.00**, up **119.25 points, or 0.38%**; and **Russell 2000 futures** were at **2,853.60**, up **2.70 points, or 0.09%**. (Economic Times, Oct. 5, 07:19 ET)[3]
